issue_context.title: Bluetooth: GATT: Written value of gatt_cf_cfg data may be dropped on power down
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The `gatt_cf_cfg` data is stored in the non-volatile memory only on `bt_gatt_identity_resolved` and `bt_gatt_disconnected`.
It is possible that device running Zephyr would drop the written value if an unexpected power down happens while connection is still maintained.
I think that, by default, the CF configuration should be stored in non-volatile memory when GATT write is handled to make sure that the default configuration is safe.

**To Reproduce**
Used nRF Desktop application (`applications/nrf_desktop`) from nRF Connect SDK (https://github.com/nrfconnect/sdk-nrf).

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Flash the nRF52840 DK with configuration that works as HID keyboard
   `west build -b nrf52840dk_nrf52840 --pristine -- -DCONF_FILE=prj_keyboard.conf`
   `west flash --erase`
2. Add logs to indicate when the following functions are called in `bluetooth/host/gatt.c`: `cf_write` (CF value GATT write), `cf_set` (CF value loaded from non-volatile memory - settings).
3. Connect and bond with a Bluetooth Central.
    Make sure that the connected Central uses GATT Caching and triggered the CF GATT write.
4. Reboot the device running Zephyr while Bluetooth connection is still maintained (before disconnection).
5. See that `cf_set` is not called after reboot, because the CF data was not stored in non-volatile memory.

Note: You can also verify that if the Bluetooth connection is disconnected before the reboot, the CF value is properly stored in the non-volatile memory for the bonded peer (and then it's restored after reboot).

**Expected behavior**
The `gatt_cf_cfg` data for a bonded peer should be stored in the non-volatile memory and restored after reboot.

**Impact**
GATT caching feature may not  work correctly - GATT Client would not be properly marked as change unaware.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
Replicated on nRF Connnect SDK (https://github.com/nrfconnect/sdk-nrf; commit hash: `54125e4ae7b670b8c8331055d8be06f8b416f5ea`).

review_comments:
Should we have something stronger than a comment to enforce this? Would a `BUILD_ASSERT` be appropriate?

Is there a way to check for existence of bits in flash in case we add more in the future and want to load from flash written to in an earlier version?
I don't think there is. I'm kinda already doing this when reading it (e.g. if the bit is not present or a bad value).

Maybe we could perform `db_hash_process` in `db_hash_commit` callback context (instead of moving it to Bluetooth long workqueue context that has low priority)?
That could allow us to avoid synchronization issues related to processing the db_hash and marking peers as change unaware when GATT database changes after a DFU operation. I think current implementation introduces possibility of accessing GATT by previously bonded peer before DB hash is processed and before the peer is properly marked as change unaware.
The issue also seem not directly related to the PR so may be addressed separately I think.

Yeah, please open another low-prio bug for that. you can assign me for now as well.
I think it should be okay to NAK all GATT access until the hash has been calculated.

Alternatively, maybe we could delay sending GATT response and force the database hash calculation in the current context (I am not sure which solution would provide better interoperability with devices available on the market)

that may be a valid idea, but this is kinda why we added this long-wq in the first place: bt runs as a coop prio, and the hash can be quite long, and will pre-empt other threads from running (even if cooperative).
Follow-up issue: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/54773
Maybe we could actually bind the function together with `sc_indicate`? When GATT database changes, we should probably always perform both operations together, right?

We should also store the information that peers that enabled robust caching are not change aware now. Otherwise it may get misaligned with db_hash (if new database hash is stored, change awareness is not and we are rebooted then after reboot we would behave as if GATT database was not changed).

> We should also store the information that peers that enabled robust caching are not change aware now

This is exactly what this function call does. Or am I misunderstanding something?

There is an edge case I think. It could appear right after the DFU.

We see that database hash does not match, so we store new hash and set change awareness to false (keep in mind the change awareness store operation is delayed). At this point we may be rebooted and after the reboot we no longer see that the database hash was modified (because new hash was already stored before the reboot), but we did not store the CF values denoting unawareness (so that peers are marked as change aware).

Should not have high impact anyway since we would most probably send SC indications (`SC_TIMEOUT` seems way shorter than timeout related to storing CCC and CF).

hm that is true, I did misunderstand you. 
The best way would be to store a "last seen hash" for each peer. I would do that if storage was free. 
I've changed it now to store to settings in `set_all_change_unaware`.

Should be good enough.
I think it's better to force a few unnecessary discoveries than to miss a necessary discovery.
This doesn't test that the write happens before the disconnection.
But also: Does anything bad happen if we power-off in the on-disconnected callback? (I suspect some work items will not run.)

I will change that so the server dies before the connection is ended.
For the second point, I think that should rather be in a separate bsim robustness-type test, since I suppose other stuff than GATT might break.
The `%p` argument shall be a pointer to void
this is a common idiom in zephyr (that we don't explicitly cast to void), take a look at e.g. `gatt.c`

C standard states that `for %p the argument shall be a pointer to void.`
Anyway let's leave it if it's acceptable here (it nearly never causes actual problems).
Nothing will be stored to flash if the device reboots/loses power before `CONFIG_BT_SETTINGS_DELAYED_STORE_MS`?

That's true. Proper fix would require to write from BT RX thread in some places I think (otherwise we never know if the value would actually be stored before response is sent). I noticed that implementation tries to avoid writing to non-volatile memory from RX thread in general (so that the issue that you spotted affects also e.g. CCC values and it used to be here before this PR too)
Yeah, not sure if there is a better way to solve it. It can anyway wait until laters as it was not introduced here as you say.
